questions.question: The Battle of Kannauj was fought between Sher Shah Suri and the Mughals led by _______________.
questions.solution:
The Battle of Kannauj (1540) was a decisive conflict where Sher Shah Suri defeated the Mughal Emperor Humayun.
  • It led to the temporary end of Mughal rule and the start of the Suri Dynasty.
  • Humayun became a fugitive for the next 15 years.

questions.question:
Arrange the following battles fought during Mughal period in correct chronological order.

a. Battle of Khanwa

b. First battle of Panipat

c. Battle of Ghaghra

d. Battle of Chausa
questions.solution:
The correct chronological order is: First Battle of Panipat (1526), Battle of Khanwa (1527), Battle of Ghaghra (1529), and Battle of Chausa (1539).
  • Babur fought the first three, while Humayun fought Chausa.

questions.question: In which year did the annexation of Awadh by Lord Dalhousie take place?
questions.solution:
The annexation of Awadh occurred in 1856 by Lord Dalhousie on grounds of 'maladministration'.
  • This was a major grievance leading to the Revolt of 1857.
  • Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Awadh.

questions.question: Which of the following Governor-Generals of British India was in favour of free press and repealed the press regulations of 1823?
questions.solution:
Lord Metcalfe is known as the 'Liberator of the Indian Press' for repealing the restrictive 1823 Press Regulations.
  • He believed in the freedom of expression to modernise India.

questions.question: In which year did Lord Dalhousie introduce the railway line in British India?
questions.solution:
In 1853, Lord Dalhousie introduced the first railway line in India, running from Bombay to Thane (34 km).
  • Dalhousie is considered the 'Father of Indian Railways'.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote Gulamgiri?
questions.solution:
Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgiri (Slavery) in 1873.
  • He dedicated the book to the American movement to free slaves, linking the condition of lower castes in India to black slaves in America.

questions.question: Dantivarman or Dantidurga was the founder of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
Dantidurga (or Dantivarman) was the founder of the Rashtrakuta Dynasty in the mid-8th century.
  • He fixed his capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed).

questions.question: Under the Charter Act of 1833 in British India, the East India Company’s monopoly on trade with which of the following countries was abolished?
questions.solution:
The Charter Act of 1833 completely ended the East India Company's commercial activities, specifically its monopoly on trade with China and trade in Tea.
  • It made the EIC a purely administrative body.

questions.question: In which amongst the following acts was Delhi declared the capital of British India in place of Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi was officially announced during the Delhi Durbar of 1911.
Note: While the answer key marks '1', historical records credit the 1911 proclamation by King George V.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts of British India did the British government take direct control of the administration of India in its own hands?
questions.solution:
Under the Government of India Act 1858, the British Crown took direct control of Indian administration from the East India Company.
  • This followed the 1857 Revolt and abolished the Dual Government.

questions.question: Which of the following acts gave the British Indian government the authority to arrest anyone without a trial?
questions.solution:
The Rowlatt Act (1919) gave the government authority to arrest and detain people without trial.
  • It was famously called the 'Black Act' (No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal).

questions.question: Which of the following was widely considered as the ‘heaven born service’ for Indians during British rule?
questions.option_1: Military service on the Burma front
questions.option_4: The Indian Civil Service or ICS
questions.solution:
The Indian Civil Service (ICS) was popularly referred to as the 'heaven born service' due to its immense power and prestige during British rule.
  • Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to join the ICS.

questions.question: Dharmapala is known to have founded which of the following universities near Bhagalpur in Bihar?
questions.solution:
Dharmapala, a powerful Pala king, founded Vikramashila University near Bhagalpur, Bihar.
  • It was a premier center of Buddhist learning alongside Nalanda.

questions.question: Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho was built under which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, the largest and most ornate in the Khajuraho complex, was built by the Chandela Dynasty.
  • It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and follows the Nagara style.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Muhammedan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh for the spread of Western education?
questions.solution:
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Muhammedan Anglo-Oriental College (1875) at Aligarh.
  • It later became the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in 1920.

questions.question: Who amongst the following became the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in December 1886?
questions.solution:
Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', presided over the second session of the INC in 1886.
  • He was also the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons.

questions.question: Diwan-i Kohi was the department of________ introduced by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.
questions.solution:
Diwan-i-Kohi was the Department of Agriculture established by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.
  • Its goal was to bring more land under cultivation by providing state loans (Sondhar).

questions.question: The Indian National Congress formally took up the Swadeshi call in its Benaras session of 1905 under the presidentship of _________.
questions.solution: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 Benaras Session where the INC formally supported the Swadeshi Movement against the partition of Bengal.

questions.question: Krishna III of Rashtrakuta dynasty established a victory pillar and a temple at which of the following cities of south India after defeating the Chola ruler Parantaka I?
questions.solution: Krishna III of the Rashtrakuta dynasty defeated the Cholas at Takkolam and established a victory pillar and temple at Rameswaram.

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements about the Indian social reformers of the 19th century is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: Mahadev Govind Ranade is associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
questions.option_2: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
questions.option_3: Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.
questions.option_4: The Aligarh Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875.
questions.solution:
The statement that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar founded the Brahmo Samaj is Incorrect.
  • The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
  • Vidyasagar is famous for his role in the Widow Remarriage Act (1856).

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Ramakrishna Mission to carry on humanitarian and social work?
questions.solution:
Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to spread the teachings of his guru and engage in social service.
  • Its headquarters is at Belur Math.

questions.question: The author of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Yahya Sirhindi claims that the founder of ________ dynasty of Delhi sultanate was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad.
questions.solution: The Sayyid Dynasty (1414–1451) claimed to be Sayyids, or descendants of the Prophet Muhammad, as recorded in Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as Tuti-e-Hind?
questions.solution:
Amir Khusro, the famous poet and musician, is known as Tuti-e-Hind (Parrot of India).
  • He is credited with inventing the Sitar and Tabla.

questions.question: Which of the following books is written by Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.solution:
'Nationalism' is a famous collection of lectures written by Rabindranath Tagore.
  • He also wrote Gitanjali, for which he won the Nobel Prize.

questions.question: Who was executed as an accomplice to the murder of AMT Jackson?
questions.solution: Krishnaji Gopal Karve was executed for his role in the assassination of A.M.T. Jackson, the District Magistrate of Nasik, in 1909.
